```{python}
#| label: spatial-completed-setup
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
from live_results import *

STATE = source_path("refine-logs/queue_spatial_1lead/queue_state.json")
LOGS = source_path("refine-logs/queue_spatial_1lead/jobs")
CATALOG = source_path("results/onelead_checkpoint_store/catalog.sqlite")
state = load_json_queue(STATE)
runs = load_spatial_training_logs("refine-logs/queue_spatial_1lead/jobs")
completed = runs.query("status == 'completed'").copy()
```

## Experiment identity

This completed legacy study is distinct from the newer 48-cell
`spatial_arch_1lead_v1` queue. It crossed ten spatial/conditioning variants,
three factorial masks (`1000000`, `1010010`, and `1110000`), and two observed
leads, yielding 60 completed training runs. Twenty-four cancelled queue entries
are retained in the queue ledger but are not model results.

Completion is verified from the training logs' terminal marker, not inferred
from the stale lock file. The checkpoint catalog independently records the
recoverable artifacts.

## Matched architecture comparisons

```{python}
#| label: spatial-completed-matched
keys = ["factorial_mask", "seed", "observed_lead"]
baseline = (completed.query("variant == @BASELINE_VARIANT")[keys + [PRIMARY_METRIC]]
            .rename(columns={PRIMARY_METRIC: "baseline_value"}))
matched = completed.merge(baseline, on=keys, how="left")
matched["pearson_improvement_over_a0"] = matched[PRIMARY_METRIC] - matched.baseline_value
display(matched.sort_values(["factorial_mask", "observed_lead",
                             "pearson_improvement_over_a0"], ascending=[True, True, False]))
fig = px.bar(matched, x="variant", y="pearson_improvement_over_a0",
             color="observed_lead", facet_row="factorial_mask", barmode="group",
             hover_name="run_name",
             title="Matched improvement in best validation Pearson over A0")
fig.add_hline(y=0, line_dash="dash")
fig.show()
```

The key reviewer controls are capacity matching and permuted geometry. A spatial
variant is physiologically credible only if it improves over A0 and the
capacity-matched control while true geometry outperforms its permutation under
the same mask, lead, seed, and training budget.

## Geometry-versus-capacity falsification tests

```{python}
#| label: spatial-falsification-controls
matrix = completed.pivot_table(
    index=["factorial_mask", "observed_lead"],
    columns="variant", values=PRIMARY_METRIC)
contrasts = pd.DataFrame(index=matrix.index)
for label, candidate, reference in [
    ("E1 − A0", "e1_panorama_film", "a0"),
    ("E1 − permuted geometry", "e1_panorama_film", "pg1_permuted_geometry"),
    ("E1 − capacity matched", "e1_panorama_film", "cm1_capacity_matched"),
    ("B1 panorama − A0", "b1_panorama", "a0"),
    ("PA1 author fusion − A0", "pa1_panorama_author", "a0"),
]:
    contrasts[label] = matrix[candidate] - matrix[reference]
display(matrix.reset_index())
display(contrasts.reset_index())

long_contrasts = contrasts.reset_index().melt(
    id_vars=["factorial_mask", "observed_lead"],
    var_name="contrast", value_name="Pearson difference")
fig = px.bar(long_contrasts, x="contrast", y="Pearson difference",
             color="observed_lead", facet_row="factorial_mask", barmode="group",
             title="Matched spatial-control contrasts")
fig.add_hline(y=0, line_dash="dash")
fig.show()
```

True E1 geometry beats permuted geometry in all six mask×lead cells by
0.0030–0.0120 Pearson and beats the capacity-matched control by 0.0024–0.0096.
The consistency of direction is evidence that the model uses the geometry
labels rather than benefiting only from parameter count.

That result does **not** establish E1 as a generally improved base. Relative to
A0, E1 gains 0.0214 only for mask `1000000`, lead I; the other five differences
range from −0.0019 to +0.0033 and are practical ties at this precision. Likewise,
simple panorama and author-fusion effects change sign across masks and leads.
The supported mechanism claim is therefore narrower: correct spatial metadata
can matter conditional on the architecture, but its average advantage over A0
is small and configuration dependent.

## Mask and observed-lead effects

```{python}
#| label: spatial-mask-lead-effects
mask_summary = completed.groupby(["factorial_mask", "observed_lead"])[PRIMARY_METRIC].agg(
    count="count", mean="mean", median="median", minimum="min", maximum="max").reset_index()
display(mask_summary)
lead_pairs = completed.pivot_table(index=["factorial_mask", "variant"],
                                   columns="observed_lead", values=PRIMARY_METRIC).reset_index()
lead_pairs["II_minus_I"] = lead_pairs["II"] - lead_pairs["I"]
display(lead_pairs.sort_values(["factorial_mask", "II_minus_I"], ascending=[True, False]))
```

Lead II is usually easier than lead I in this internal validation study, but
that difference combines information content, preprocessing, and the set of
missing targets. It is not proof that lead II is intrinsically superior for
every downstream task. Increasing the mask from `1000000` to `1110000` also
raises absolute Pearson for most variants, so spatial comparisons must remain
within mask rather than attributing cross-mask gains to architecture.

## Claim ledger

| Claim | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Correct geometry is used by E1 | Supported descriptively | E1 exceeds permuted geometry in all six matched cells. |
| Gains are only extra capacity | Disfavoured | E1 exceeds the capacity-matched control in all six cells. |
| E1 is the improved base architecture | Not supported | Five of six E1−A0 differences are ties near zero; one lead/mask cell drives the visible gain. |
| Lead II is universally the best input | Not established | Internal averages favour II, but endpoint and external-cohort transport remain separate questions. |
| Spatial conditioning improves clinical delineation | Requires external evidence | These logs contain reconstruction validation metrics only. |

## Interpretation limits

- All cells use seed 42; there is no between-seed uncertainty estimate.
- Metrics are validation screening metrics extracted from logs, not a common
  held-out per-record ledger.
- Lead I and lead II effects may differ and remain separately reported.
- External RDB results for these checkpoints are analyzed in the following
  chapter, where waveform, boundary, and region metrics are available.
